Tactical.threat: a direct threat to win material next move, or a piece that is attacked and must move or be defended
Tactical.defense: defending an attacked piece, pawn or square, or parrying a threat
Tactical.pin: a piece cannot or should not move because a more valuable piece or the king stands behind it; breaking a pin
Tactical.fork: one piece or pawn attacks two or more targets at once (double attack)
Tactical.skewer: a valuable piece is attacked and moving it exposes a piece behind it on the same line
Tactical.discovered_attack: moving one piece uncovers an attack or check by another
Tactical.removing_defender: capturing, deflecting, decoying or overloading a defender
Tactical.hanging_piece: an undefended piece or pawn that can simply be taken
Tactical.trapped_piece: a piece with no safe square that can be won
Tactical.combination: a forcing sequence of checks, captures and threats that wins something
Tactical.sacrifice: material deliberately given up for an attack, initiative or other gain

King.mate_threat: checkmate is threatened, forced or close (mating net, mate in N)
King.back_rank: a king trapped on its back rank by its own pawns; back-rank mate threats
King.king_attack: an attack aimed at the king and its shelter
King.king_safety: how safe a king is: exposed, weakened or well protected shelter
King.castling: castling, the side to castle on, losing or preventing castling
King.perpetual_check: an endless series of checks forcing a draw

Positional.outpost: a strong square for a piece, usually a knight, that enemy pawns cannot attack
Positional.weak_square: a hole or weak square or colour complex the opponent can use
Positional.center_control: control or occupation of the central squares, including a pawn center
Positional.space: having more space or being cramped
Positional.open_file: an open or half-open file and the rooks or queen using it
Positional.seventh_rank: a rook or queen on the opponent's second rank
Positional.diagonal: a bishop or queen on an open or long diagonal, or a battery along it
Positional.piece_activity: how active pieces are: their scope, mobility and good squares
Positional.passive_piece: a passive, misplaced or restricted piece with little scope
Positional.bad_bishop: a bishop hemmed in by its own pawns on its colour
Positional.bishop_pair: having both bishops against bishop and knight or two knights
Positional.piece_coordination: pieces working together: connected or doubled rooks, batteries
Positional.prophylaxis: a move made mainly to stop the opponent's idea before it happens

Dynamics.development: bringing pieces into play in the opening; a lead or lag in development
Dynamics.tempo: gaining or losing time, e.g. developing with an attack or wasting moves
Dynamics.initiative: one side dictates play, making threats the other must answer
Dynamics.pressure: sustained pressure on a target (pawn, square, file or king) without an immediate win
Dynamics.counterplay: the defending side's own active chances or counterattack
Dynamics.trades: exchanging pieces or queens, simplifying or liquidating
Dynamics.complications: a sharp, unclear or double-edged position

Pawns.pawn_structure: the pawn structure as a whole, its strengths and weaknesses
Pawns.weak_pawn: a pawn that is hard to defend and can be targeted
Pawns.isolated_pawn: a pawn with no friendly pawns on the adjacent files
Pawns.doubled_pawns: two pawns of one side on the same file
Pawns.passed_pawn: a pawn with no enemy pawns ahead of it on its own or adjacent files
Pawns.promotion: a pawn about to queen, the queening square, or a pawn race
Pawns.pawn_break: a pawn advance that challenges or opens the pawn structure
Pawns.pawn_storm: advancing several pawns against the enemy king
Pawns.pawn_majority: more pawns on one wing, or a minority attack
Pawns.blockade: a piece standing in front of an enemy pawn to stop it

Material.material_advantage: one side is ahead in material
Material.winning_material: the move or a forced line wins material
Material.compensation: non-material assets that make up for missing material
Material.blunder: the move is a serious mistake that loses material or the game
Material.advantage: one side is clearly better or winning, beyond counting material
Material.draw: a drawn or drawish position: repetition, fortress, stalemate, equality

Endgame.endgame: the endgame itself or steering into one
Endgame.king_activity: an active king used as a fighting piece, usually in the endgame
Endgame.opposition: kings facing each other with one square between them
Endgame.zugzwang: any move worsens the position of the side to move
